subject.title: Stuck-session liveness monitor misclassifies healthy processing runs as stale during event-loop stalls

question: Should OpenClaw change the processing/no-activeWorkKind recovery policy now, or require live/deterministic proof that healthy runs can lose activity bookkeeping during event-loop stalls?
rationale: The source path is real and shipped, but current tests intentionally rely on it for stale processing recovery and the issue's healthy-run abort chain is still reported as likely rather than confirmed.

options.title: Require proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open until a targeted stall repro shows a healthy active run reaching stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run.

options.title: Patch classifier now
options.body: Approve a narrow classifier/recovery change for processing sessions and redesign the existing stale-processing recovery tests around the new policy.

options.title: Fold into active-run recovery
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader false active-run abort cluster and resolve it through the canonical recovery/progress work.

recommendation.title: Require proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a targeted stall repro shows a healthy active run reaching stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent recovery work in the same subsystem makes this the best available routing candidate for the proof-versus-policy choice.
